newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portuguese shares end weaker 1st time in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Portuguese shares end weaker 1st time in 1997.

text.p: 1720 GMT - Portuguese shares closed weaker for the first time in 1997, ending the day 1.5 percent down. The weakness of other markets pulled down Lisbon bourse, dealers said.
* Shares in cement group Cimpor closed down one percent after surging at the start of the session to an all-time high of 3,925 escudos on news it had acquired two Brazilian cement businesses.
* Portugal Telecom, after rising 27 percent in the first two weeks of 1997, ended the session down 2.6 percent.
* Dealers said activity tomorrow would depend on the close of Wall Street today.

* "The drop of the market was purely and simply a technical correction, which served as a breather," said one dealer. "The market's positive fundamentals are not in doubt. December inflation data was good news." He added: " I think that tomorrow could be a calmer session with some investors taking a rest."
